column1: # LERENA AND LLERENA ACROSS THE RIVER PLATE - measured 13 September 2026 in the FamilySearch
# FULL-TEXT corpus, which reads handwriting across un-indexed images and covers both Montevideo
# and Buenos Aires (but NOT Santa Fe).
# METHOD: search the bare surname as an exact phrase, open the Place filter, expand South America,
# and read the per-country counts off the facet. Anyone can repeat it in two minutes.
# WHY A CONTROL IS NEEDED: the two national corpora are not the same size, and every surname has its
# own geography. So two reference surnames were measured the same way, and the comparison is made
# against THEM rather than against an assumed corpus ratio.
surname
LERENA
LLERENA
Fernandez (reference)
Bustamante (reference)
# *** WHAT IT SAYS. ***
# Both reference surnames run ARGENTINA-HEAVY - one by 2x, one by 8x. So does LLERENA, by 3.6x.
# LERENA runs the other way, and hard: SIX TIMES MORE COMMON IN URUGUAY THAN IN ARGENTINA.
# It is the only one of the four that reverses. And it is the spelling this family used.
# *** WHAT IT DOES NOT SAY. *** It is a measurement of a digitised corpus, not of a population.
# Full-text coverage is uneven between countries and periods, and handwriting recognition misreads.
# It is evidence about where the NAME lives, not about where any particular family lived, and it
# cannot place Juan Carlos Lerena anywhere. Filed as a distribution argument, which is what it is.
# Note also how neatly it sits with Sancho Llerena Aguilar, the Cordoba soldier who married at
# Canelones in 1791 and whose descendants' name is spelled BOTH ways in the Uruguayan registers:
# the Uruguayan branch shed the double L, and the Argentine bearers of the name kept it.
